report.summary: Corrected: the default broker is now the MQTT listener (mqtt://homeassistant.gdenu.fi:1883), not the Home Assistant web port 8123; the TLS form is mqtts://…:8883 and is a one-field change on /settings. Builds at 2.94 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: You are right: 8123 is Home Assistant's own web UI, not a broker listener. Aiming the default URI there could never answer an MQTT session, so the default is now mqtt://homeassistant.gdenu.fi:1883 — the Mosquitto add-on's plain MQTT port.

If the household's add-on exposes only the TLS listener, the correct URI is mqtts://homeassistant.gdenu.fi:8883; that is a one-field change on /settings and needs no rebuild, so I did not guess which listener is open — the settings page now states the distinction (broker port ≠ HA web port) and its placeholder follows the new default.
The certificate name-check skip is untouched and still applies only to TLS URIs (mqtts:// or :8883), with the chain verified against the built-in pack or a supplied CA.

openQuestions: Which listener your Mosquitto add-on actually exposes (1883 plain, 8883 TLS, or a custom port) is only visible from the add-on's configuration; set it once on /settings and it is stored in NVS from then on.
